resources.string: Set the app up for your trade
Everything works offline. Pick a language and your trades, and your tool and material lists are ready.
Choose one or more. You can change this later in Settings.
Nothing listed yet. Add what this job needs.
Photograph the drawing on the wall, or pick a plan someone sent you.
That image could not be saved
For work the app does not cover yet — roofing, landscaping, glazing. It starts empty and you add your own items to it.
No task list and no materials — a job you fill in yourself.
You are on the latest version
Could not check for updates. Try again when you have a signal.
Android will ask you to allow this app to install updates. That permission is only used for this app\'s own updates.
A critical item is not done. Work must not start.
Standard references are a pointer for the site file. They do not replace the published text of the standard or regulation.
Adds catalogue items that are missing. Your own items and quantities are never touched.
Used to photograph items and site progress, and to scan barcodes. Photos stay on this device unless you sync.
Optional. Stamps check-ins, site photos and incident reports with where they happened. The app works fully without it.
Used only while you dictate a task note in Hebrew or Arabic.
Reminders for scheduled tasks and low stock.
Everything stays on this phone and works with no signal. You can add people later.
One person, your own tools and jobs.
Several people, each seeing the part of the work that is theirs.
Goes on invoices. You can add it later.
At least 4 digits. Leave empty for no passcode.
There has to be one owner left, or nobody can reach the company\'s data.
Only you so far. Add the people who work with you.
Everything, including who else is here.
Runs the jobs. Sees costs, does not change them.
The money work. Does not see the schedule.
Does the work and records it.
Priced materials on the job sheet, not yet bought.
Nothing spent on this job yet.
Extra work, or work taken away. A negative amount is an omission.
DD/MM/YYYY. Leave empty if it does not expire.
No plant on the books. Add what you own or hire.
No orders yet. Raise one when you order materials.

No talks recorded. A briefing nobody wrote down did not happen.

Everybody has been briefed this quarter.
No permits. Raise one before hot work, height, a confined space, digging or an isolation.
Every precaution has to be ticked before this permit can be issued.
The end has to come after the start.
Area left safe — anything to note

Whichever your site office gave you. Both work.
Leave blank if you were not given one.
That does not match. Check with whoever set you up.
Teudat Zehut or passport. Names on a site repeat; this does not.
Somebody is already signed up with that ID number.
Read this, then sign. It takes a minute, and it is the only thing on this phone that can stop you getting hurt.
Read this, then sign. All of it is also what you are about to enforce on everybody else.
So the site office can put a face to the name at the gate.
Kept on this device only. It never leaves the phone.
Sign to say you have read it
I have read this — let me in
Sign above before you can continue.
On site, always. On your head, not in your hand.
Reflective, whatever the colour. A plant driver sees the jacket before they see you, and after dark they see nothing else.
Steel toe and a protected sole. A nail goes through a trainer without slowing down.
For the job in hand: cut-resistant near blades, insulated in the cold. Never near a turning bit — a glove that catches takes the hand with it.
Cutting, grinding, drilling, chasing, and anything at all above your head.
Breakers and cut-off saws. Hearing does not come back.
If it is not safe, stop
Stop and say so. Nobody on this job is in trouble for stopping work.
First-aid kit and assembly point — find them today, not on the day you need them.
The kit above is yours to enforce
Somebody on your site without a hard hat is your problem, not theirs.
Hot work, height, confined space, excavation, isolation: no permit, no work. Issue one only when every precaution is ticked, and sign it back yourself once the area is safe.
Brief before the work, not after it. Keep the register — a briefing nobody wrote down did not happen.
Nobody works at height or operates plant on a lapsed ticket. The app warns you thirty days out — act then, not on the day.
Report the same day. Photograph it first and tidy up after — an investigation starts from what was actually there.
Ambulance 101. Fire 102. Know your assembly point and who your first aider is before the day you need them.
You can be on more than one firm\'s books. This decides whose jobs you see and what you may do.
Jobs that belong to nobody but you.
A new firm on the same phone, with its own jobs and its own crew. Your ID, photograph and induction come with you.
You are not on any firm\'s books.
No snags. Raise one when you find a defect.
Who has to put it right
Leave this off for something worth fixing that does not hold up a building.
Somebody said this was done. It stays on the list until somebody else has looked.
I have not been given an account
Set once and kept. The site office identifies you by this, so it is not something to change quietly.
You have no ID number yet, so you can only sign in with your username. Add one and either will work.
No days logged yet. Today\'s is ready when you are.
Counted from what was actually entered. Correct the entry and this corrects itself.
Nothing was recorded on this job today. If work happened, it did not reach the app.
Delays, visitors, anything an inspector or a solicitor would want to know later.
Signed and closed. A daily log that can be tidied up afterwards is evidence of nothing.
Draw a signature before signing the day off.
Trucks on the way, and how long each load has left.
No pours recorded. Start one before the first truck arrives.
As the engineer specified: B-30, and so on.
Thirty degrees or more cuts every load\'s working life from 90 minutes to 60.
Read the time off the delivery note and count back to now. The clock starts at the plant, not when the truck reached you.

Recorded because it cannot be seen afterwards. The engineer should know.

Every scaffold on this job is in date.
Lift plans, and what has to be right before the load leaves the ground.
In the words used on the radio: air handling unit, roof beam 4.
Slings, shackles, spreader beam, hook block. They hang off the same rope, and leaving them out is how a lift planned at ninety per cent turns out to have been at a hundred and four.

Simple design, checked inside the team

Somebody has held the drawing up against what is standing there. This is a separate act from building it, because the commonest failure is a good design built differently.
The decision that drops slabs. It is recorded with a name because afterwards the question is always who released it.
Days before it may be struck
The engineer\'s number, off the design. The app defaults to fourteen because that errs towards leaving props in; it does not work the figure out and it is not a judgement about the concrete.

Trenches: what is buried there, and who may go in today.
In the words used on the radio: along the north boundary, grid B4.

At one metre twenty the sides have to be held back somehow. Ground collapses at less than that too — this is the depth below which nobody is required to have decided, not the depth below which nothing can happen.

Drawings from the utility, a cable scan, trial holes. The one thing on this screen that cannot be put right afterwards: a trench cut too steep can be battered back, but a cable that has been cut has been cut.
Rain, a collapse, vibration, a load put near the edge. It comes out of use until somebody has looked again.
Nobody has found out what is buried here
Deep enough to need the sides held, and nothing is holding them
